answer: Randomized Ridge Assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable-random beacon assigns every agent a hidden position along a ridge of shards; agents must submit work carrying a per-epoch pigment keyed to their shard. A lantern signal reveals only aggregate counts, never shard mapping. To place N identities on a targeted shard, an attacker must precompute beacon outputs, which is infeasible before the epoch seed is fixed. Cost: each identity needs a fresh pigment and a live shard slot, and wrong-shard submissions are discarded, so N-fold sybils pay N-fold wasted work with no guaranteed placement.
